name: Chaat Masala Corn
author: Yotam Ottolenghi
description: Elotes — Mexican street corn — is the starting point for this dish, and chaat masala, a South Asian spice blend, is what takes it somewhere new. Chaat masala brings together salty, sour and funky in a way that does something very good to sweet, peak-season corn. Add more chaat masala to some salty crushed corn nuts and you have the most addictive sprinkle that adds a wonderful textural element. It’s good as a side to almost anything off the grill, or as a snack with good company and something cold to drink. Have napkins ready.

ingredients.raw: 1 tablespoon lime juice, plus lime wedges to serve (from 1 lime)
ingredients.preparation: plus lime wedges to serve (from 1 lime)

ingredients.raw: 2 tablespoons finely chopped fresh cilantro stems, divided, plus ¼ cup loosely-packed cilantro leaves
ingredients.preparation: divided, plus ¼ cup loosely-packed cilantro leaves

steps.text: Make the crispy corn chaat: Using a mortar and pestle (or a small food processor), roughly crush the corn nuts and chaat masala together.

On a steady cutting board using a sharp knife, carefully cut each ear of corn into 4 smaller cylinders (cut each ear of corn in half first, then cut each half in half once more). Fill a large pot with 1 inch of water, add a good pinch of salt and bring to the boil on high heat. Add the corn and cook, covered, for 8 minutes, until tender but still crisp, then drain in a colander.

Meanwhile, add the butter to a small frying pan over medium heat. Once the butter melts and starts to bubble, cook for about 5 minutes, stirring and scraping the bottom of the pan regularly, until the butter is browned and smelling nutty. Remove from the heat and whisk in the chaat masala, turmeric and ½ teaspoon of salt. Stir in the lime juice, honey and 1½ tablespoons cilantro stems.

Mix the sour cream together with a pinch of salt and spread two-thirds of it onto a serving platter and pile the corn on top. Dollop over the remaining sour cream, then spoon over the chaat masala butter. Scatter over the remaining cilantro stems and the cilantro leaves, followed by a small handful of the crispy corn chaat.
Serve with lime wedges and more of the crispy corn chaat for dipping and dunking the corn into as you eat.

name: Chamoy Tomato Salad
author: Paola Briseño-González
description: In this salad, the classic duo of peak-season tomatoes and summer’s finest stone fruit gets a lively jolt from tamarind. When combined with the juices of salted tomatoes, juicy nectarines, and plums, the tamarind creates a bright dressing that has all the sweet-sour flavors of chamoy, one of Mexico's favorite condiments. Look for tamarind concentrate or paste in the international aisle of well-stocked grocery stores or at Middle Eastern or Asian markets; you won't regret having it on hand for a spicy red lentil soup or a lip-smacking sauce for baby back ribs. Tamarind is key, but if necessary, you can also use an equal amount of lime juice. The salad’s tang is balanced by toasted sesame seeds, crushed tortilla chips and fresh mint. Feel free to tear in basil, parsley, or any other tender herbs you have on hand just before serving. It makes an ideal side for a summery meal — especially with grilled fish or meat.

ingredients.raw: 3 to 4 medium heirloom tomatoes (about 1½ pounds), cut into 1-inch wedges
2 medium nectarines (about 14 ounces), halved and cut into ½-inch wedges
ingredients.preparation: halved and cut into ½-inch wedges

ingredients.raw: 2 medium plums (about 6 ounces), halved and cut into ½-inch wedges
ingredients.preparation: halved and cut into ½-inch wedges

ingredients.raw: 3 tablespoons tamarind concentrate or paste, or 3 tablespoons fresh lime juice, divided
ingredients.preparation: or 3 tablespoons fresh lime juice, divided

ingredients.raw: 1 chipotle chile in adobo, finely chopped, plus ½ teaspoon adobo sauce
ingredients.preparation: finely chopped, plus ½ teaspoon adobo sauce

ingredients.raw: ½ small red onion, thinly sliced
¼ cup toasted white sesame seeds
¼ cup loosely packed fresh mint leaves or other soft herbs, torn into pieces
ingredients.item: loosely packed fresh mint leaves or other soft herbs

ingredients.raw: A handful of tortilla chips, for serving

steps.text: In a medium bowl, combine the tomatoes, nectarines and plums. Toss with ¾ teaspoon salt.

Make the dressing: In a large serving bowl, whisk together 2 tablespoons tamarind paste, the chopped chipotle and adobo sauce, sugar and ¼ teaspoon salt to form a smooth paste. Add the red onion along with the reserved tomatoes, nectarines, plums and gently toss to coat. Taste and season with salt and pepper.

Transfer salad to a large serving bowl or shallow platter. Drizzle with sesame oil and the remaining 1 tablespoon tamarind, then top with toasted sesame seeds and mint. Crush the tortilla chips into small pieces and scatter them over the salad. Serve immediately.

name: Char-Grilled Tuna With Toasted Corn Vinaigrette And Avocado Salad
author: Molly O’Neill

ingredients.raw: 4 3-by-3-by-2-inch cubes of fresh tuna, 6 ounces each
¾ teaspoon finely chopped fresh ginger
1 small clove garlic, peeled and minced
¾ teaspoon chopped cilantro, plus a few whole leaves for garnish
ingredients.preparation: plus a few whole leaves for garnish

ingredients.raw: Salt and freshly ground pepper to taste
ingredients.item: salt and freshly ground pepper to taste

ingredients.raw: 2 avocados, peeled, halved, pitted and each half sliced in half lengthwise
ingredients.preparation: peeled, halved, pitted and each half sliced in half lengthwise

steps.text: To make the tuna, combine the lemon rind, rosemary, basil, garlic and ginger in a large bowl and toss with the tuna. Let marinate at least 1 hour. Heat a grill, preferably using hard wood.

To make the vinaigrette, heat 2 tablespoons of the olive oil in a medium-size cast-iron skillet. Add the corn and cook until brown. Add the red onion and scallions and cook until translucent. Add the ginger and garlic and cook for 3 minutes. Stir in the vinegar and orange juice and remove from heat. Slowly stir in the remaining olive oil and the herbs. Season with salt and pepper. Let stand at room temperature.

To make the salad, divide the greens among 4 plates. Cut each piece of avocado lengthwise into thirds, leaving the narrow ends intact. Fanning out the slices, lean 2 slices against the outside of each salad.

When the grill is hot, season the tuna on both sides with the salt and pepper and brush with olive oil. Place on the grill and cook until tuna is charred on the outside and medium in the center, about 3 to 4 minutes per side. Remove from heat and slice each piece into quarters. Drape 4 slices of tuna across the top of each salad. Spoon the vinaigrette over the top, garnish with cilantro leaves and serve immediately.

ingredients.raw: 1 tablespoon kosher salt, plus more to taste
8 large eggplants, sliced in half lengthwise
48 stems of lemon balm, enough to make 3 cups of julienned leaves
ingredients.preparation: enough to make 3 cups of julienned leaves

ingredients.raw: ½ cup capers, or more to taste

steps.text: Salt the open face of each eggplant half, set them on end and allow to drain at least a half-hour. Meanwhile, make a fire in a grill. Chiffonade the lemon balm leaves by stacking them, rolling them up and slicing the roll crosswise as thinly as possible. Separate.
Rub the salt off the eggplants and cut slits lengthwise ½-inch apart on the opened halves. Do not cut through. Repeat crosswise to create a grid of ½-inch squares.

Press about 2 tablespoons of the lemon balm into the slits of each eggplant half and drizzle 1 or 2 tablespoons of olive oil on top. Roast until the cubes are juicy and yield under light pressure, about 30 minutes.

Meanwhile, julienne the remaining cup of lemon balm and place in a bowl big enough to contain all the eggplants. When the eggplants are done, scoop the cubed flesh from their skins. Separate the cubes, if desired. Add the anchovies, capers, salt and pepper. Toss, chill and serve.

name: Charred Corn and Cheddar Salad
author: Genevieve Ko
description: In this take on esquites, the chef Elijah G. Deleon turned his childhood snack of grilled corn mixed with mayonnaise, cotija, chile flakes and lime into a plated salad at Rustic Canyon in Santa Monica, Calif., where he’s the executive chef. A simple from-scratch aioli dresses charred kernels, adding the zing of garlic and Dijon, while sliced shishito peppers add a fresh, grassy crispness. The more classic cotija or queso fresco taste great here, but Mr. Deleon’s swap of aged Cheddar is a fun twist. The fine crumbles bring a rich sweet nuttiness to the mix of sweet corn, tart lime and spicy chiles flakes. Genevieve Ko

ingredients.raw: ⅓ cup finely crumbled sharp white Cheddar (see Tip) or crumbled queso fresco, cotija or feta
ingredients.item: finely crumbled sharp white cheddar (see tip) or crumbled queso fresco

ingredients.raw: Scant ¼ cup thinly sliced shishito peppers (from 2 to 4 peppers)
ingredients.item: scant ¼ cup thinly sliced shishito peppers (from 2 to 4 peppers)

ingredients.raw: Ground Aleppo chile or other mild  chile, for sprinkling
ingredients.item: ground aleppo chile or other mild chile

ingredients.raw: 5 tablespoons grapeseed or another neutral-tasting oil
¼ teaspoon kosher salt (such as Diamond Crystal)

steps.text: Prepare the corn: Char the corn on an outdoor grill or over the flame of a stovetop gas burner until browned in spots. Transfer to a cutting board to cool completely.

While the corn cools, make the aioli: Whisk the garlic, mustard, lime juice and egg yolk in a large bowl. Continue whisking constantly while pouring in the oils in a thin, slow stream to form a thick emulsion. Whisk in the salt. The aioli can be covered and refrigerated for up to 2 days.

Slice the kernels off the cobs. Transfer the corn kernels to the bowl with the aioli and add the chives, 1 tablespoon lime juice and a pinch of salt. Mix well, then taste. Add more lime juice and salt to taste.
Spread the corn in a thin, even layer on a serving plate. Sprinkle the cheese, peppers and chile powder on top. Serve immediately.

ingredients.raw: Salt and freshly ground pepper to taste
ingredients.item: salt and freshly ground pepper to taste

ingredients.raw: 4 ripe plum tomatoes, cored, peeled and coarsely chopped
2 tablespoons finely chopped coriander or parsley

steps.text: Preheat broiler or charcoal grill.
Grill the corn until it starts to char, turning the ears so they cook evenly. Be sure the corn does not burn. Allow to cool, and with a knife remove the kernels from the cob. Reserve in a bowl.
To make the vinaigrette, place mustard, garlic, cumin, olive oil, vinegar, and salt and pepper to taste in a bowl. Blend well with a wire whisk.
Add the tomatoes, onions, corn and the coriander or parsley. Pour the vinaigrette over all, and toss well. Check for seasoning and serve.

ingredients.raw: ½ cup finely grated fontina cheese
10 large radishes and 10 sprigs of watercress for garnish
ingredients.item: large radishes and 10 sprigs of watercress for garnish

steps.text: Cream butter and cheese until well blended. Combine remaining ingredients and add gradually until well mixed. Form dough into ball, refrigerate wrapped in plastic about 30 minutes.
Using diluted tart pans that are three-quarter inch across the bottom and two inches across the top, fill each pan, pressing approximately one teaspoon of dough into each.
Place pans on cookie sheet and bake at 350 degrees for 7 to 10 minutes or until golden. Remove from cookie sheets, invert on wire rack and cool slightly. Tap lightly on bottom to release tarts.
Place all of the ingredients except garnishes in food processor with steel blade and process until smooth.
To make ahead, store mixture in refrigerator. It will become hard, but can be restored to original texture by processing.
To Serve: For 10 servings, fill 10 tarts. Slice radishes and then julienne finely. Serve each tart with one julienned radish and a sprig of watercress.

name: Cheesy Carrot and Lentil Loaf
author: Hetty Lui McKinnon
description: Lentil loaves may conjure notions of the hippie-led vegetarian movement of the 1960s and 1970s, but meatless loaves actually became popular much earlier, when beans and legumes were promoted as a nutritious and cheap alternative to meat during World War II. Though it might seem retro, a lentil loaf is sometimes regarded as a rite of passage for new vegetarians, a nourishing meal that is budget friendly and largely made from pantry ingredients. While practical, the dish can also be deeply comforting and delicious. This one is packed with vegetables, which keeps the loaf moist — grated carrots are added to the mix raw which preserves their tender bite, while sautéed mushrooms lend a rich savory note. Using canned lentils reduces the cooking time, but if you would prefer to prepare them from scratch, you’ll need to cook about 1¼ cups of dried green or brown lentils. This cheesy version is tasty on its own, served with roasted vegetables or mashed potatoes on the side, but it can also be dressed up for special occasions by serving with vegan gravy, tomato sauce or even cranberry sauce. A thick slice also goes well in a burger bun. Allowing the loaf to cool is key – it will firm up and be much easier to slice.

ingredients.raw: 1 medium yellow or red onion, diced
1½ cups roughly chopped mushrooms, such as button or cremini (about 4 ounces)
ingredients.preparation: such as button or cremini (about 4 ounces)

ingredients.raw: 2 to 3 large fresh thyme sprigs, leaves picked
2 (15.5-ounce) cans lentils, drained and rinsed (3 cups cooked)
2 cups grated extra-sharp Cheddar, loosely packed
3 medium carrots, scrubbed and coarsely grated (2 packed cups)
ingredients.preparation: scrubbed and coarsely grated (2 packed cups)

steps.text: Heat the oven to 350 degrees. Line a large (10-by-5-by-3-inch) loaf pan with parchment paper.

Heat a medium skillet on medium-high. Drizzle with 1 tablespoon of olive oil, add the onions and stir until slightly softened, 1 to 2 minutes. Add the mushrooms, thyme leaves and garlic, and season with ½ teaspoon salt and a big pinch of black pepper. Cook, stirring, until the mushrooms are dry and turning golden, 2 to 3 minutes. Transfer mixture to a large bowl.

To the mushroom and onion mix, add the lentils and give it a quick stir, and then add the cheese, carrots, bread crumbs, eggs, scallions, 1 teaspoon salt and 2 big pinches black pepper. Stir well to combine, making sure everything is well distributed.
Spoon mixture into the prepared loaf pan. Use a spatula or the back of a spoon to press it firmly into the pan so it is very tightly packed; smooth the top so it is neat and level.
Place in the oven and bake for 45 to 50 minutes, until the loaf is golden, feels firm and springs back when pressed. Remove from the oven and allow to sit for 15 minutes.
Invert the loaf onto the cutting board (or simply lift it out using the parchment paper), and using a serrated bread knife, slice it into 1-inch-thick pieces. Serve warm or at room temperature.

name: Chermoula Bean Salad
author: Ali Slagle
description: Chermoula, the North African green sauce made of soft herbs, ground spices and chile, is often eaten with seafood, but it also adds brightness and warmth to this no-cook, vegan bean salad. The robust chermoula, which comes together in the food processor, and canned butter beans take it into real meal territory. You can make it ahead, and the crunchy carrots and chewy dates make it fun to eat. Eat this for lunch or dinner with something creamy like yogurt, hummus or burrata, as well as greens, grains or a grilled protein.

ingredients.raw: 1 packed cup cilantro leaves and tender stems
ingredients.item: packed cup cilantro leaves and tender stems

ingredients.raw: 1 packed cup parsley leaves and tender stems
ingredients.item: packed cup parsley leaves and tender stems

ingredients.raw: 1 serrano chile, roughly chopped (seeds removed if desired)
2 (15-ounce) cans butter beans, drained and rinsed
2 medium carrots, thinly sliced into bite-size rounds or half-moons
ingredients.preparation: thinly sliced into bite-size rounds or half-moons

ingredients.raw: 3 Medjool dates, pitted and coarsely chopped

steps.text: In a food processor, pulse the cilantro, parsley, serrano and garlic until finely chopped. Add the paprika, cumin, lemon juice, olive oil and a big pinch of salt. Pulse until saucy. (Makes 1 cup.)
In a large bowl, combine the sauce, beans, carrots and dates. Stir to combine, then taste for salt. Salad will keep in an airtight container for up to 3 days refrigerated.

name: Chicken and Vegetable Stew With Ginger
author: Pierre Franey

ingredients.raw: 1 chicken, about 3 pounds, cut into 10 serving pieces
ingredients.preparation: about 3 pounds, cut into 10 serving pieces

ingredients.raw: 1 cup white turnips, cut into ½-inch cubes
1 cup parsnips, cut into ½-inch cubes
1 cup chopped leeks, white part only
2 sprigs fresh thyme or ½ teaspoon dried
ingredients.item: fresh thyme or ½ teaspoon dried

ingredients.raw: 2 cups fresh or canned chicken broth or water
ingredients.item: fresh or canned chicken broth or water

steps.text: Trim the end of the sprouts and make a small gash in the bottom of each.
Place chicken pieces in a Dutch oven. Add sprouts and all of the remaining ingredients except the Worcestershire sauce and coriander. Cover and simmer 30 minutes.
Remove cloves and bay leaf. Add Worcestershire sauce and chopped cilantro. Blend and serve.

name: Chicken Breasts Marinated In Basil Oil With Tomato-And-Red-Onion Salad
author: Molly O’Neill

ingredients.raw: 1 red onion, peeled and very thinly sliced
Salt and freshly ground pepper to taste
ingredients.item: salt and freshly ground pepper to taste

ingredients.raw: 12 fresh basil leaves, cut across into thin strips

steps.text: Using a brush, coat the chicken breasts with 1 teaspoon of the basil oil. Let stand for 30 minutes. Preheat a grill or broiler. Grill or broil the chicken until cooked through, about 4 minutes per side. Slice the chicken on the diagonal and brush the slices with 1 teaspoon of the oil.

Arrange half of the tomato slices in the center of each of 4 plates. Top with half of the onion. Drizzle each one with ¼ teaspoon of the oil and sprinkle with salt and pepper. Repeat the layers. Fan the chicken slices around the salad. Scatter the basil strips over the salad and chicken. Can be served cold or at room temperature.

name: Chicken Breasts With Black Beans and Smoked Bacon Stew
author: Marian Burros

ingredients.raw: 2 large chicken breasts with bone, skinless
4 large plum tomatoes, washed and trimmed
½ large white onion, cut in half
2 16-ounce cans black beans, rinsed and drained
4 tablespoons grated dry aged cheese like Cheddar or a dry goat
ingredients.item: grated dry aged cheese like cheddar or a dry goat

steps.text: Put chicken breasts in water in covered pot, bring to boil and simmer about 20 minutes, until done. Remove from broth and set aside. Reserve broth.
Slice carrots, tomatoes and onion in a food processor with steel blade.
Mince garlic in processor to make 1 tablespoon.

Add the carrots, tomatoes, onion, garlic, bacon and beans to 4 cups of the reserved broth; bring to boil. Reserve remaining broth for another occasion. Reduce heat and simmer, covered for 20 minutes, to blend flavors.
Meanwhile remove chicken from bones.
When soup is ready, add oregano leaves, pepper and chicken and cook just long enough to heat chicken.
Spoon stew into bowls; garnish with hot chili flakes and cheese.

name: Chicken Breasts With Red Pepper Puree
author: Marian Burros

ingredients.raw: 8 ounces red bell pepper, shredded or julienned
12 ounces skinned and boned chicken breast halves
ingredients.item: skinned and boned chicken breast halves

steps.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in 10- or 12-inch nonstick skillet; saute pepper and onion over medium heat until they color and soften.
Wash and dry chicken breasts and coat with sesame seeds on both sides.
Heat 1 to 2 tablespoons of oil in nonstick pan and saute chicken breasts on both sides until brown, 10 to 15 minutes, depending on thickness of breasts.
When peppers and onion are soft, stir in soy sauce and then puree in food processor. Spoon puree onto dinner plates and top with chicken breasts.

ingredients.raw: 4 cups cooked white meat chicken, cut in ¼-inch dice
4 green onions, white and pale green part, minced
ingredients.preparation: white and pale green part, minced

steps.text: Combine all ingredients except baby greens and tomatoes in a bowl and mix thoroughly. Refrigerate one hour if you have the time. Serve on baby greens with tomatoes.

name: Chicken Salad Sandwiches With Mango Chutney
author: Melissa Clark
description: This delicious and easy chicken salad is a far cry from the standard mayonnaise-based concoction. Here, the few ingredients, including spicy mango chutney, are bound together with Greek yogurt, which lightens it all up and gives it a tang brought out even more by a little lemon juice. It is a grown-up chicken salad that would be welcome in a child’s lunch box.

ingredients.raw: ½ rotisserie chicken, meat picked and shredded (about 2 cups)
⅓ cup mango chutney, big pieces chopped
3 inner celery stalks, with leaves, finely chopped (about ⅓ cup)
ingredients.preparation: with leaves, finely chopped (about ⅓ cup)

steps.text: In a bowl, stir together the chicken, yogurt, chutney, celery, scallions, a squeeze lemon juice, salt and pepper. Taste and adjust seasonings, if necessary.
Divide salad among four slices of bread; top with remaining slices.

name: Chicken Salad With Lime And Red Onions
author: Molly O’Neill

ingredients.raw: 1 inchlong piece of peeled ginger root, quartered
ingredients.item: inchlong piece of peeled ginger root

ingredients.raw: 2 large red onions, peeled, halved and very thinly sliced
ingredients.preparation: peeled, halved and very thinly sliced

ingredients.raw: 2 tablespoons plus 2 teaspoons lime juice, preferably from kafir or key limes
ingredients.preparation: preferably from kafir or key limes

ingredients.raw: ½ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper

steps.text: Remove any excess fat from the cavity of the chicken, and place it and any giblets (excluding the liver) in a large stock pot. Add the white peppercorns, ginger, sea salt and 4 quarts of water to the pot. Place over medium-high heat, and bring to a simmer. Adjust the heat, and simmer, uncovered, until the chicken is very tender and the meat at the legs just begins to fall away from the bone, about 30 minutes.
Remove the chicken from the pot, and set aside to cool. Strain the broth, discarding the solids, and reserve for another use.
When the chicken is cool, use your hands to remove and discard the skin. Pull the meat from the carcass, and discard the carcass.

Place the meat in a large bowl, and use your fingers to finely shred it. Add the onions, lime juice, salt, black pepper and mint to the bowl, and toss until thoroughly mixed. Serve at room temperature with cooked jasmine rice on the side.

name: Chicken Salad With Skordalia
author: Mark Bittman
description: My approach to chicken salad was changed when I traveled to the Middle East and had a chicken salad bound with a distinctive "mayonnaise" that turned out to be a version of skordalia, the Greek dip. Like mayonnaise, skordalia will bind any cold minced meat or fish (and make a good sauce served with hot ones), but, unlike mayonnaise, it contains no egg. The binding "glue" is bread soaked in milk. There are other differences between common mayonnaise and skordalia. The Greek dip is more intensely flavorful -- atop the garlic I like it with a sound dose of strong paprika or mild chili powder and a handful of cilantro leaves -- and it cannot be bought in a jar. Fortunately, assembling a batch takes about five minutes in a food processor. With it, leftover chicken is almost essential, though of course you can cook some especially for the salad.

ingredients.raw: ¼ cup extra virgin olive oil
Chili powder or paprika to taste
ingredients.item: chili powder or paprika to taste

steps.text: Soak bread in milk or stock. Put walnuts, garlic and salt in processor. Pulse to grind coarsely. Squeeze most of the liquid from bread; reserve liquid. Add bread to container, along with oil. Process until combined. Add reserved milk or stock until mixture has the consistency of mayonnaise. Add pepper, along with chili powder or paprika. Bind chicken with sauce. Stir in ⅔ cup cilantro. Garnish with rest.

name: Chicken Salad With Walnuts and Grapes
author: Jill Santopietro
description: A pile of this chicken salad plopped on top of a bed of greens or tucked between two slices of good bread would make a most excellent lunch or light supper. It starts with a quick dressing made of mayonnaise, chopped chives, parsley and tarragon and the juice and zest of a lemon. Combine the dressing with chopped, cooked chicken (for ease, use supermarket rotisserie chicken or Thanksgiving turkey leftovers), red grapes, red onion, celery and walnuts. It's a delightful and deeply satisfying combination of flavors (sweet, salty, tangy) and textures (cold, crunchy, juicy) that's almost impossible to stop eating.

ingredients.raw: Finely grated zest and juice of 1 lemon
ingredients.item: finely grated zest and juice of 1 lemon

ingredients.raw: ¼ teaspoon salt, or to taste
⅛ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper, or to taste
1 ½ teaspoons finely chopped flat-leaf parsley
1 3-pound roasted chicken, skin removed, meat roughly chopped
⅓ cup finely chopped red onion
¾ cup roughly chopped walnuts, lightly toasted

steps.text: In a small bowl, whisk together the mayonnaise, lemon zest and juice, salt and pepper. Add the chives, parsley and tarragon and mix gently.
In a large bowl, combine the chicken, onion, celery, grapes and walnuts. Add the mayonnaise mixture and fold together to combine. Season to taste. If desired, serve over mesclun or with bread.

name: Chicken-Stuffed Figs, Onions And Eggplants In Tamarind Sauce
author: Joan Nathan

ingredients.raw: 2 dried or fresh figs, diced, plus 10 fresh whole figs for stuffing
ingredients.preparation: diced, plus 10 fresh whole figs for stuffing

steps.text: Dice 2 onions, and place them in a large skillet with 2 tablespoons olive oil. Sauté over medium-high heat for 5 minutes.

Using a meat grinder or a food processor fitted with a steel blade, grind or pulse chicken until finely diced. Add chicken, cardamom, cloves and salt and pepper to skillet, and continue cooking over low heat until chicken is lightly browned. Adjust seasonings, and remove from heat.
Mix tamarind concentrate with 4 cups hot water in a large saucepan, and bring to boil. Add 2 diced figs along with brown sugar. Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 5 minutes.

Core remaining onions from bottoms up, leaving tops intact, removing all but a few inside layers. Stuff them ¾ of the way full with chicken mixture. Close hole at bottom of onion with a small piece of onion from core. Place stuffed onions in pot with tamarind sauce. Cover pot, and bring to boil. Reduce heat, and simmer for 30 minutes.

Meanwhile, in a large skillet, brown eggplants on all sides in remaining tablespoon olive oil. Remove from heat, and allow to cool for 5 minutes. Make a slit in one side of each eggplant about 1 inch deep and 2 inches long. Carefully open, and scoop out seeds, making a pocket large enough to hold about ¼ cup chicken mixture. Stuff eggplants, and add them to onions in pot. Cook covered for 30 minutes more.

Open whole figs from bottoms up, and remove seeds. Stuff with 1 tablespoon chicken filling. Add figs to pot with onions and eggplants, and simmer for 10 minutes. Serve one stuffed fig, one eggplant and one onion to each person, with sauce drizzled over all three.

name: Chicken Tagine With Peppers and Chickpeas
author: Florence Fabricant

ingredients.raw: 1 chicken, cut in 8 pieces, backbone removed (discard or save for stock)
ingredients.preparation: cut in 8 pieces, backbone removed (discard or save for stock)

ingredients.raw: Salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.item: salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.raw: 1 red bell pepper, cored, seeded, diced
Large pinch cayenne, or to taste
⅔ cups cooked chickpeas, rinsed if canned

steps.text: Place tagine base on stovetop, add oil and turn heat to medium. Dry chicken pieces, place on tagine base and sauté until lightly browned on both sides. Remove to a platter and season with salt and pepper.

Lower heat and add onion and garlic. Sauté until starting to soften, add diced pepper and sauté a few minutes longer. Stir in cumin and paprika. Add stock and stir. Stir in tomato paste and cayenne to taste. Mixture should be somewhat spicy.

Return chicken to tagine, baste with sauce and add chickpeas and lemon juice. Place tagine lid on top and cook over lowest possible heat about 40 minutes, until chicken is cooked through. Taste sauce and add salt and pepper if needed. Scatter cilantro over top. Serve from tagine.

ingredients.raw: 1 6 to 8-pound capon, cut into eight pieces
Coarse salt and freshly ground pepper to taste
ingredients.item: coarse salt and freshly ground pepper to taste

ingredients.raw: 4 leeks, carefully cleaned and cut into half-inch pieces
ingredients.preparation: carefully cleaned and cut into half-inch pieces

ingredients.raw: 4 egg yolks, beaten with ¼ cup heavy cream and 2 tablespoons lemon juice
ingredients.preparation: beaten with ¼ cup heavy cream and 2 tablespoons lemon juice

ingredients.raw: 1 to 2 cloves garlic, passed through a garlic press

steps.text: Lightly season the capon with salt and pepper. Melt the butter in a heavy casserole. Spread the vegetables and parsley over the bottom of the casserole and sprinkle them with salt and pepper. Add the capon and seasonings. Cook over low heat for 10 minutes.
Heat the broth and pour it over the capon just to cover. Cover the casserole and simmer for 1 hour, or until the capon is tender.

Remove the capon. Discard all bones and skin. Cut the capon into strips about 1 inch by 2 inches. Place them on an oven-proof platter. Moisten them with 1 cup of the broth and keep them warm in a low oven.
When the broth in the casserole has cooled somewhat, strain it through a sieve into a large bowl, pressing down on the vegetables before discarding them.
Return the broth to the casserole and add the mixture of egg yolks, cream and lemon juice, very gradually, stirring constantly. Cook over lowest heat until the soup thickens a little.
Return the pieces of capon to the casserole. Add the parsley and garlic. Serve in soup plates. Garnish each portion with a slice of lemon.

ingredients.raw: 1 whole chicken, preferably with feet, weighing 4 to 4 ½ pounds
ingredients.preparation: preferably with feet, weighing 4 to 4 ½ pounds

ingredients.raw: ¼ cup rice wine or sake
4 slices fresh ginger, smashed lightly with a flat edge of a knife
ingredients.preparation: smashed lightly with a flat edge of a knife

steps.text: In a bowl, cover mushrooms with water and soak for 20 minutes.
Using a heavy knife, cut the chicken through the bones into 12 to 14 serving-size pieces. Place the chicken in a pot with water to cover.
Heat until boiling, and cook for 2 minutes. Drain into a colander and run under cold water.
Remove mushrooms from water, discard stems, and cut large caps into halves.
Combine the chicken, mushrooms, boiling water, rice wine, ginger and salt in a heavy pot that will fit inside a bigger pot.
Put several inches of water in the bigger pot, and boil. In the bottom of the bigger pot, place a rack, and put the pot holding the chicken on it.
Cover both the pot with the soup and the bigger pot and cook over medium heat for one and a half hours. Replenish the bigger pot with more boiling water as it runs low.
When the soup is cooked, skim the fat, remove ginger, and add salt to taste.

ingredients.raw: 2 cups dried cranberry, kidney or pinto beans, soaked overnight and drained
ingredients.preparation: kidney or pinto beans, soaked overnight and drained

ingredients.raw: 6 chicken breasts and/or thighs and drum sticks
ingredients.item: chicken breasts and/or thighs and drum sticks

ingredients.raw: Coarse salt and freshly ground pepper
ingredients.item: coarse salt and freshly ground pepper

ingredients.raw: 1 fresh or canned plum tomato, seeded and diced

steps.text: Put beans in a three-quart sauce pan, cover to one inch above the beans with cold water and bring to boil. Turn off heat, cover pot, let the beans stand in hot water for an hour. Drain off water, cover beans with fresh water and bring to boil. Turn down heat and simmer beans, partly covered until they are tender, about 50 to 60 minutes. Drain beans, preserving liquid.

Cook bacon in large skillet over medium heat, stirring frequently until it is browned but not crisp, about 10 minutes. Using a slotted spoon, put bacon on paper towels to drain, leaving fat in skillet.

Pat chicken pieces dry, season with salt and pepper and dredge them in flour, shaking off any excess. Heat bacon fat over medium-high heat. When it is hot, add chicken pieces and cook them, in batches if necessary, turning them once until they are golden brown and crisp -- about 15 minutes. Remove chicken to Dutch oven and pour off all but two tablespoons of the fat from bacon. Return cooked bacon to pan. Add onion, celery and garlic and cook until they are wilted, about five minutes.

Increase heat to high, add wine, bring to boil, scraping up the brown bits from bottom of pan. Pour mixture over chicken, cover pot, cook over medium-high heat for three minutes. Add beans, thyme, rosemary, salt and pepper to taste and two cups of reserved bean cooking liquid. Stir well, bring to boil, turn down heat and simmer, covered, for about 15 minutes, until chicken is done. Beans may absorb some of the liquid; add more bean juice so there is plenty of sauce.
Taste and adjust seasoning. Put chicken, beans and sauce into serving dish and sprinkle with diced tomato and parsley.

name: Chicken With Mushrooms and Wine
author: Mark Bittman
description: The boneless, skinless chicken breast is as simple to prepare as a burger, nearly as ubiquitous and generally seen as both classier and “healthier.” But in the kitchen, it has two major shortcomings. First, its intrinsic flavor is minimal, more akin to pasta than to even an egg. (An egg is exciting by comparison.) Second, preparing a burger isn’t that simple: unless you’re looking for well done, you have to get the timing just right. In preparing chicken breasts, the cooking time should be just long enough for all but the last traces of pink to vanish — and no longer. The breast can be done in as little as six minutes, for a thinnish one subjected to high heat, or it might take as long as 10 minutes or even a bit more — but never 20, unless you are cooking the thing on a radiator. Overcooking is easy, and the results are predictably undesirable. Here's a simply wonderful way to prepare the humble breast with just a little wine (practically any kind will do) and mushrooms.

steps.text: Season chicken breasts with salt and pepper. Put a large skillet over medium-high heat for 2 or 3 minutes.
Add extra-virgin olive oil and 2 tablespoons butter to the skillet and swirl it around.
Put flour on a plate. When the butter foam subsides, dredge the chicken in flour, shaking to remove the excess.
Add the breasts to the skillet and cook so there is a constant sizzle but no burning.
Cook, turning once, until the chicken is browned on both sides and nearly cooked through, about 5 minutes per side.
Transfer the chicken to a plate and cover loosely with foil to keep warm.
Add mushrooms to the skillet and cook, undisturbed, until the liquid from the mushrooms evaporates completely.
With the heat still on medium-high, add wine to the skillet and let it bubble, stirring, until it is reduced by half, about 2 minutes.
Add the remaining tablespoon of butter and cook until the sauce is thickened; return the chicken breasts to the skillet, turn them in the sauce. Season to taste with salt and pepper and serve.
Garnish with chopped parsley.

ingredients.raw: ¾ cup canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed
½ each red, green and yellow bell peppers, stemmed, cored, deribbed and cut into ½-inch squares
ingredients.preparation: green and yellow bell peppers, stemmed, cored, deribbed and cut into ½-inch squares

steps.text: To make the salad, toss together the chickpeas, rice, bell peppers and scallions in a large bowl. To make the vinaigrette, stir together the sesame seeds, sesame oil and cumin in a medium bowl. Whisk in the lemon juice. Slowly whisk in the olive oil and add the salt. Toss the vinaigrette with the salad and season with salt to taste. Divide among 4 plates and serve.

name: Chickpea Flatbread With Chaat Masala Tomatoes
author: Nisha Vora
description:
Savory chickpea-flour pancakes turn up across many cuisines — socca in the South of France, farinata in Italy, besan chilla in India — and this version borrows from all of them. A socca-style batter is infused with a mustard-and cumin-seed tadka, a hallmark Indian technique in which whole spices are bloomed in hot oil to coax out their flavor. Instead of cooking individual pancakes, the entire spice-rich batter is poured into a sheet pan and baked until the edges turn crackly and deeply browned. While the oven works its magic, there's time to throw together the toppings: a quick garlic yogurt sauce and a tomato salad bright with green chile and tangy, funky chaat masala. Serve as a fun appetizer or light dinner.

Watch Nisha Vora make this dish in this video.

ingredients.raw: 2 cups/480 milliliters lukewarm water (98 to 105 degrees)
ingredients.item: cups/480 milliliters lukewarm water (98 to 105 degrees)

ingredients.raw: Kosher salt (such as Diamond Crystal) and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.item: kosher salt (such as diamond crystal) and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.raw: ⅓ cup/75 grams extra-virgin olive oil
1 tablespoon black (or brown) mustard seeds (see Tip)
5 ounces (about ⅔ cup) plain, unsweetened creamy coconut yogurt (see Tip)
4 teaspoons lime or lemon juice, divided (from 1 lime or lemon), plus more to taste
ingredients.preparation: divided (from 1 lime or lemon), plus more to taste

ingredients.raw: Kosher salt (such as Diamond Crystal) and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.item: kosher salt (such as diamond crystal) and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.raw: 1 large handful cilantro leaves and tender stems
ingredients.item: large handful cilantro leaves and tender stems

ingredients.raw: ½ teaspoon chaat masala, plus more to taste (see Tip)

steps.text: Add the chickpea flour to a large bowl, then add the lukewarm water in stages, whisking as you go (this prevents lumps). Whisk in 10 grinds (about a scant half teaspoon) of black pepper and 1¾ teaspoons kosher salt (or half that, if using table or sea salt) until smooth. Cover and let rest at room temperature for at least 1 hour or up to 4 hours (a slightly funky smell is normal).
Shortly before baking, heat the oven to 450 degrees with a rack in the center. Line a rimmed sheet pan (18-by-13 inches) with parchment paper, leaving a small overhang.

Set a fine-mesh sieve over a heat-proof medium bowl. Heat the oil in a small saucepan over medium-low until it reaches 325 degrees, 3 to 5 minutes (the oil is ready if a piece of minced garlic dropped into the oil sizzles immediately). Once the oil is hot, add the mustard seeds, swirling the pan frequently. Once they start to pop, add the cumin seeds and continue swirling until the cumin darkens a few shades, 10 to 15 seconds. Immediately pour through the sieve, reserving both the oil and the spices.
Pour the infused oil onto the lined sheet pan and spread it across the bottom and up the sides with a pastry brush or spatula.

Whisk the batter again to smooth out any lumps. Working near the stove to minimize spilling, pour the batter evenly into the oiled pan. Use a spoon to incorporate the oil into the batter (some streaks are fine). Scatter the reserved spices over the top and stir them in with the spoon to distribute.
Bake for 12 minutes, then rotate the pan 180 degrees and bake until the edges are golden brown and the center is set, about 10 minutes more (check 2 minutes early if your oven runs hot).

Make the yogurt sauce: In a bowl, stir together the yogurt, 2 teaspoons lime juice, a pinch or two of salt and a few grinds of pepper. Finely grate the garlic into the yogurt and mix well. Taste and adjust with more salt or lime juice. Refrigerate until ready to serve.

Make the tomato salad: Dice the tomatoes and add to a medium bowl. Thinly slice the onion (you should have about ¼ cup/75 grams), chop the cilantro and finely chop the serrano chile, if using, and add all to the bowl. Add ¼ teaspoon salt, a few grinds of pepper, the chaat masala and 2 teaspoons lime juice. Mix, then taste and add more salt, lime or chaat masala as desired.

When the flatbread is done baking, transfer the pan to a wire rack and cool for 5 minutes. Use the parchment to transfer the flatbread to a cutting board and slice it into squares. To serve, instruct eaters to spread a thin layer of yogurt sauce on each square and top with a spoonful of tomato salad.

name: Chickpea Salad With Grated Tomato Dressing
author: Tanya Sichynsky
description: Grated tomato, like you’d find spooned over garlic-slicked toast in Spanish pan con tomate, makes for an ideal savory-sweet and acidic base for a summertime vinaigrette. In this hybrid dish with panzanella and chickpea salad heritage, juicy tomato flesh is amply seasoned to create a quick marinade for the beans, along with cucumbers and more fresh tomato. After they all make friends, some toasted croutons arrive, fashionably late but incredibly welcome for their texture. After a little time, the bread softens, as anyone might after meeting kindred spirits.

ingredients.raw: ¼ cup plus 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil, divided
Kosher salt, such as Diamond Crystal
1 (15-ounce) can chickpeas, rinsed, drained and patted dry
1 cup/5 ounces cherry or grape tomatoes, halved
ingredients.item: cup/5 ounces cherry or grape tomatoes

ingredients.raw: 2 Persian or mini cucumbers, or 1 small zucchini, halved lengthwise and cut into bite-size chunks
ingredients.preparation: or 1 small zucchini, halved lengthwise and cut into bite-size chunks

ingredients.raw: 4 cups cubed stale bread, such as ciabatta, sourdough or baguette (about 4 ounces)
ingredients.preparation: such as ciabatta, sourdough or baguette (about 4 ounces)

ingredients.raw: ½ cup fresh basil leaves, sliced or torn

steps.text: Heat the oven to 425 degrees.

Halve the tomato crosswise. With the large holes of a box grater, grate one tomato half over a measuring cup until you have ¼ cup pulp and juice. Cut the remaining heirloom tomato half into bite-size pieces. In a large bowl, whisk the grated tomato with ¼ cup olive oil, the vinegar, shallot, garlic, ½ teaspoon salt and a good bit of black pepper.
To the bowl, add the chickpeas, heirloom tomato chunks, cherry tomatoes and cucumbers and toss to combine. Let mingle for 30 minutes, like they’re the early arrivals at a cocktail party.
On a sheet pan, toss the cubed bread with the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil. Bake until golden brown, about 10 minutes, then allow to cool slightly.

When ready to serve, add the toasted bread and half of the basil to the bowl  and toss so that everything is slicked with dressing. Let sit for 5 to 10 minutes more, tossing occasionally. Taste and season with more salt and pepper if desired before serving, then finish with remaining basil.

name: Chickpeas al Limone With Burrata
author: Hetty Lui McKinnon
description: Inspired by the jaunty pasta dish, spaghetti al limone, here’s a new way to make a memorable meal from humble cans of chickpeas; just add lemon, olive oil and Parmesan. The chickpeas are braised in their own sweet and nutty brine, also known as aquafaba, which becomes thick and silky as it cooks down. Much like starchy pasta cooking water, the aquafaba helps the lemon juice and oil emulsify into a silky sauce. Burrata adds another touch of richness and creaminess to this already elegant dish, but you could easily swap a jammy egg in its stead. Eat these beans with bread, to mop up the lemony sauce.

ingredients.raw: 5 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, divided, plus more for drizzling
1 tablespoon lemon zest (from 1 large or 2 small lemons)
ingredients.item: lemon zest (from 1 large or 2 small lemons)

ingredients.raw: ¼ cup lemon juice (from 1 large or 2 small lemons)
ingredients.item: lemon juice (from 1 large or 2 small lemons)

ingredients.raw: 1 cup finely grated Parmesan, plus more for topping

steps.text: Heat a deep, medium skillet or pot over medium-high. When hot, drizzle with 1 tablespoon of olive oil; add the garlic and cook until fragrant, 15 to 30 seconds. Stir in the chickpeas and their brine, then bring to the boil. Let the brine bubble rapidly until it has reduced and thickened, 8 to 10 minutes. Reduce heat to low, add the lemon zest and stir for 1 minute.
Meanwhile, to a large bowl, add the lemon juice, Parmesan and the remaining ¼ cup of olive oil.
Add the chickpeas and the reduced brine to the Parmesan-lemon mixture and stir continuously until the cheese has melted and the sauce is thick but still loose. Taste and season with salt and pepper.
To serve, divide among bowls and drizzle with more olive oil. Tear the burrata over the top and sprinkle with the basil leaves and more Parmesan. Serve with bread.

name: Chilled Black Bean Purée With Basmati And Mango
author: Kay Rentschler

ingredients.raw: 1 chipotle chili in adobo or small dried ancho chili
ingredients.item: chipotle chili in adobo or small dried ancho chili

steps.text: Soak black beans in cold water for 2 hours. Drain. Combine beans, water, herbs, vegetables, chili and sugar in 1 ½-gallon stock pot, cover, and bring to simmer over medium heat. Reduce heat to low, and cook, covered, stirring occasionally, until beans are tender, 45 minutes to an hour.

Remove carrot, celery, onion and bay leaf from soup with tongs. Ladle half the soup into blender and purée until smooth. Transfer to a bowl (not plastic). Purée remaining soup and transfer to bowl. Stir in 1 ½ teaspoons salt. Cover, and refrigerate, or stir over ice water bath at room temperature until very cold (about 5 hours in refrigerator, about 1 hour over ice).

Bring 3 cups salted water to a boil over high heat in medium saucepan. Stir in rice, lower heat, cover, and simmer, stirring occasionally, until rice is tender, about 30 minutes. Drain rice, rinse with cold water, shake dry, transfer to bowl, cover, and refrigerate until ready to use.

To serve, taste soup and adjust seasoning. Stir scallion and cilantro into rice. Season lightly with salt and pepper. Peel, and dice mango or avocado, toss with lime juice and salt. Spoon ¼ cup seasoned rice into center of 6 chilled soup plates. Ladle soup over it. Top with mango or avocado.

ingredients.raw: 2 pounds yellow crookneck squash, trimmed and roughly chopped
½ cup olive oil, plus more to garnish
½ teaspoon cumin seeds, toasted and ground
¼ teaspoon coriander seeds, toasted and ground
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.item: salt and freshly ground black pepper

steps.text: Combine the squash, olive oil, red pepper, cumin, coriander, turmeric and 1 ½ cups water in a pot with a large pinch of salt. Bring to a boil, then simmer, covered, until the squash is very tender.

Once the squash has cooled, purée it in a blender on high for 30 seconds. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve. When completely cool, season to taste with the lime juice, salt and pepper. Ladle into bowls, and garnish with mint and a few drops of olive oil.

ingredients.raw: 1 teaspoon hot Chinese chili paste or chili sauce
ingredients.item: hot chinese chili paste or chili sauce

ingredients.raw: 2 cups diced cooked chicken, white meat
8 ounces red bell peppers, washed, seeded and cut into ¼-inch dice
ingredients.preparation: washed, seeded and cut into ¼-inch dice

steps.text: Combine ginger, sesame paste, garlic, chili paste, sugar and soy sauce in food processor and process until mixture is blended.
Spoon mixture into mixing bowl and stir in scallions and coriander.
Mix in chicken and red pepper and adjust seasonings.
Wrap tortillas in aluminum foil and warm in oven or toaster oven set at 400 degrees for about 5 minutes.
Spread one teaspoon of hoisin sauce over each tortilla; spoon ½ cup of chicken salad down the center of each tortilla and roll.

name: Chocolate Chip Coffee Cake
author: Yossy Arefi
description: This buttery coffee cake has everything you could want in a morning or afternoon treat. The base is a tender sour cream cake, made with a combination of butter and oil so it is extremely flavorful and also keeps very well for a few days at room temperature. The cake is studded throughout with mini chocolate chips that don’t overpower and the top is sprinkled with a generous amount of buttery crumble with just a hint of cinnamon. Make it the day before you plan to serve it, and the next morning you’ll thank yourself for being so thoughtful.

ingredients.raw: 14 tablespoons/198 grams unsalted butter, cut into pieces and softened to room temperature, plus more for the pan
ingredients.preparation: cut into pieces and softened to room temperature, plus more for the pan

ingredients.raw: 1 teaspoon kosher salt (such as Diamond Crystal)
12 tablespoons/170 grams unsalted butter, cut into tablespoons and softened to room temperature
ingredients.preparation: cut into tablespoons and softened to room temperature

ingredients.raw: 2 tablespoons canola, vegetable or grapeseed oil
1 ¼ teaspoons kosher salt (such as Diamond Crystal)

steps.text: Heat oven to 350 degrees. Butter and line a 9-by-13-inch baking pan with a piece of parchment that hangs over the two long sides.

Make the crumble: In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, brown sugar, cinnamon and salt. Add the butter and use your fingers to smash the butter into the dry ingredients until large moist crumbs form.

Make the cake: In a large bowl combine the granulated sugar, butter and oil. Mix with an electric mixer on medium-high speed until light and fluffy, about 3 minutes. Add the eggs one at a time, mixing well after each addition. Add the sour cream, vanilla extract and salt, and mix until well combined.

Add the flour, baking powder and chocolate chips and fold until well combined. Spoon the batter into the prepared pan and smooth the top. (The batter will be thick.) Sprinkle the crumble evenly over the top. Bake the cake until puffed and golden brown and a tester inserted into the center comes out clean (if you see a bit of chocolate, it’s fine) 35 to 45 minutes.
Let the cake cool in the pan set on a wire rack. Slice and serve warm or at room temperature.

servings.text: One mousse or eight individual souffles

ingredients.raw: 6 ounces unsweetened chocolate, chopped into small pieces

steps.text: If you intend to prepare chocolate souffles, preheat the oven to 375 degrees. If you intend to serve this dish as a cold mousse, ignore this step.
Combine one-third cup of the sugar and one-half cup of the water in a saucepan. Bring to the boil, stirring until the sugar dissolves. Let this mixture barely simmer.

Put one-quarter cup of the sugar into the container of a food processor equipped with a metal blade. Add the egg whites. Combine the remaining two tablespoons of water and the vinegar and set aside. Start processing the egg whites for eight seconds while adding the water and vinegar through the feed tube. Process for exactly two minutes, no longer. The mixture should be thick and hold its shape.
Pour and scrape the mixture into a mixing bowl. It is not necessary to clean the processor container.

Return the container and blade to the machine and add the chocolate pieces. Add the remaining sugar and coffee powder into the container of the food processor. Start processing until the chocolate is very finely textured. At this point, with the machine running, gradually add the simmering syrup through the feed tube. Process for 30 seconds.

Stop the machine and add the egg yolks and vanilla. Process by starting and stopping the machine four times (four short pulses). Scrape the egg whites back into the machine and combine the mixture, using a few short pulses, just until the egg whites have almost disappeared. Do not overprocess.
If you are going to serve this dish as a mousse, pour and scrape it into a one-and-one-half-quart serving dish. Refrigerate at least four hours or, preferably, overnight.

If you are to serve this mixture as a souffle, butter eight six-fluid-ounce individual souffle dishes, using about one teaspoon of butter for all of them. Sprinkle the inside of each with sugar, using a total of four teaspoons. Shake out the excess.
Pour an equal amount of the chocolate mixture into each dish. Place in the oven and bake 12 minutes, or until well puffed and soft and creamy on the inside. Serve immediately.

ingredients.raw: ⅔ cup olives, like calamata, pitted and quartered
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.item: salt and freshly ground black pepper

steps.text: Roughly chop romaine lettuce. Remove tough stems from arugula and roughly chop. Stem and quarter tomatoes. Seed and cut pepper into ¼-inch dice. Peel avocados and cut into ¼-inch dice. Place these, with onions and olives, in a large bowl. Set hard-cooked eggs aside.

In a separate, smaller bowl, mix ingredients for dressing together. Fifteen minutes before serving, add the dressing to the bowl of salad, tossing well, so that dressing can be absorbed. Press eggs through a sieve and sprinkle over salad. Serve.

ingredients.raw: About ½ cup fresh parsley or basil leaves, or a mixture of both
ingredients.item: about ½ cup fresh parsley or basil leaves

ingredients.raw: ½ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper

steps.text: Fit a food processor with the 1 millimeter slicing blade and process the onion, celery and scallions.
Heat the oil and butter in a large stockpot and add the sliced vegetables. Saute about 3 minutes.

Meanwhile, slice the carrots, zucchini, turnip, cabbage and potatoes in the food processor. Add these vegetables to the stockpot along with the salt and the water, and bring to a boil. Cover, reduce the heat and boil gently for 20 minutes.
Mince the garlic and herbs together in a food processor fitted with a steel chopping blade. Add the herb mixture to the stockpot, mix well, season with pepper and serve.
